summary: This study systematically investigates how enhancer pairs combine to regulate promoters using a three-way combinatorial MPRA in mouse embryonic stem cells. Analysis of ~69,000 enhancer-promoter combinations reveals that enhancers generally combine near-additively across multiple developmental promoters. Surprisingly, promoter strength modulates the response non-linearly, with weaker promoters showing supra-additivity. A housekeeping promoter exhibited a distinct, more limited dynamic range. These findings indicate that enhancer integration is mostly additive, but promoters transform these signals in a context-dependent, non-linear manner.

notes.why_it_supports: This quote directly supports the core finding that enhancer pairs typically act additively in mammalian genomes.
